angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 8,202,303 km at 38.05 pc = 2.88 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48455: distance 38.052 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.006), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 38.052 +/- 0.228 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 26.0971 +/- 0.1974 mas (same row, RUWE 1.79), 132.2 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 11.79 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48455: radius 11.79 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 51.395 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.056) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 8,202,303 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4504 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48455: effective temperature 4504 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.077) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 48455: effective temperature 4504 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.077) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
